title: Hold a hanging lamp's shade still with one hand while the other screws a bulb into its socket
instruction: Hold the hanging lamp's shade still by its rim with one hand, and with the other take the bulb from its holder and screw it into the lamp's socket until it is seated, then let go with both hands.
context: Changing a light bulb is one of the most common household jobs, and one that older and disabled people often need help with. A lamp hanging on chains swings and spins as soon as its bulb is turned, so one hand steadies the shade while the other screws the bulb in.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A loose hanging lamp (uplight), 500 g: a shallow drum shade of white opal glass, 30 cm across and 5 cm tall with a wall 8 mm thick, centred 28 cm forward on the centre line, its underside 3 cm above the table, hung on three brass chains (from the rim front left, back and front right) from a fixed ceiling rose 70 cm above the table; it swings and spins freely. An empty socket stands in the shade's middle, facing up: a dark tube 2.6 cm across, its mouth 6.5 cm above the table. (2) A loose slim tubular bulb, 30 g: a glass tube 1.8 cm across and 4 cm long, domed on top, on a brass screw cap 1.5 cm across and 1.8 cm long. It stands cap down in a fixed dark holder (a base 5 x 5 cm and a ring 1.2 cm tall) 20 cm forward, 22 cm right. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. Caught: the thread catches when the cap's tip is in the socket's mouth (up to 12 mm deep, within 6 mm of its axis, lined up within 12 degrees) and the bulb is turned a quarter turn clockwise (seen from above) against the lamp; turns count net from then, and each draws the bulb 8 mm in. Seated: caught, with the cap's tip at least 15 mm into the socket. Let go: both grippers' fingertip centres (TCPs) at least 3 cm from the middle of the bulb's glass and from the shade's rim. 1.0: seated and both let go; 0.5: caught and turned at least 1 turn in; 0.25: caught; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with the lamp and the bulb still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Unscrew the bulb, stand it back cap down in its holder, and let the lamp hang still.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the lamp hangs from a ball joint (the chains are rigid), its swing damped, its spin free. PhysX has no screw thread: once the bulb catches, a joint keeps it on the socket's axis, drags as they turn against each other (0.3 N m s/rad) and draws it 8 mm in per turn; the bulb does not collide with the lamp. The bulb does not light. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
